
=================================================================
#62 Kangrim  (태초)  [FLASHBACK EPISODE]
Arc: The Fall of Euija · tone: psychopomp ritual
Logline: A diver drowns, and the island tells its last story: the strongman who went down alive to arrest the judge of the dead, and the crow that lost the book of everyone’s hour.
=================================================================
[0] ¶ On this island, a death gets a fire on the shore and one story.
[1] ¶ This winter it is the diver who grilled his fish. She went down at the third rock and did not come up. Gyebek was in the water with the others until dark, counting other people’s breaths.
[2] Gyebek: She was twenty-six. / Her mother is on the shore.
[3] Yuri Dora: She is.
[4] Gyebek: That is the wrong order.
[5] Yuri Dora: It is. Sit, Turtle. The island keeps one story for last, and this is why.
[6] Yuri Dora: Now the last one. / Kangrim. / Heaven did not send him.
[7] ¶ A rich couple killed three brothers for their silk and sank them in a pond. The brothers came back, and died again, and no living court could try a case like that. So the magistrate, a man called Gimchi, sent his strongest man down to fetch the judge of the dead.
[8] Gyebek: How did they come back.
[9] Yuri Dora: Three flowers on the water. Three beads. Three sons. Don’t ask, that part takes a whole night. / And yes, Gimchi. Don’t laugh. He was a serious man.
[10] Gyebek: I was not going to laugh.
[11] Gyebek: …He sent a living man to arrest the judge of the dead.
[12] Yuri Dora: He did.
[13] ── SCENE: The Road Down ──
[14] ¶ His wife kept the gate-god and the kitchen-god fed, so they put him on the road. At the last pond he shut his eyes and jumped, and stood up at the underworld gate. Someone was already walking that road with a red book. Haewonmek, the oldest fetch there is. Kangrim asked the way. Haewonmek pointed, and kept walking. Kangrim waited, and addressed King Yumla with court courtesy.
[15] Kangrim: Your Majesty. The living court requests you. / There is a case. Living law cannot close it.
[16] [CARD Yumla: The judge of the dead. Every ledger in the dark ends on his desk.]
[17] Yumla: Go home. / I will come at the hour I name.
[18] ¶ He came. The pond dried. The bones came up. The three brothers went home to their parents. The couple who had killed them did not. **Yumla** keeps the sentence. Then he turned to the magistrate and asked to borrow the man who had fetched him.
[19] Yumla: Lend me that man. I still have errands.
[20] Yuri Dora: The magistrate refused. He did not believe in a soul. / So they split him. The magistrate kept the body. Yumla took the soul.
[21] ¶ That is how Kangrim died upstairs and woke as a fetch of the dead. The living official kept the half he could see. Death kept the other half.
[22] Gyebek: …They divided a man.
[23] Yuri Dora: They both wanted him.
[24] ¶ Yumla then put in his hands a ledger that told each living person their hour — eighty, and in order, the old before the young. On the way down Kangrim trusted it to a crow. The crow set the book on a wall to eat at a slaughter-field. A snake swallowed the writing. Caught, the crow cried a new rule so the blame would not sit on one bird: parents after children, children after parents. Since then the hour does not come in a just order.
[25] ❝QUOTE (Chasa Bonpuri (차사본풀이) recited by Go Yeon-ok (고연옥), recorded by Gang Jeong-sik, Gang So-jeon and Song Jeong-hui, 2011 — Sanggari, Aewol-eup; sung as Cheseo Bonpuri (체서본풀이) (Hanguk Gubimunhak Daegye, rev. ed.)): “Give me the red writ. When it’s the old one’s turn, let the child come. When it’s the child’s turn, let the old one come. I’ll bring them back like water running uphill, out of order.”❞
[26] ¶ One errand was left: a man who had dodged death for three thousand years. Kangrim sat in a stream washing charcoal until the old man stopped to laugh at him, and took him by the sleeve. Only then did Yumla seat him as the one who comes for everyone else. That is why he asks a question at the threshold. Not for the sentence — Yumla keeps the sentence. A scrambled list still deserves accurate last words.
[27] Kangrim: I do not punish. / I collect — for His Majesty. / Since the list was scrambled, nobody knows the hour until I am already in the room.
[28] Gyebek: …Then a man can die before his king, and the book still opens.
[29] Yuri Dora: The book went wrong on the road. The walk did not. / That is the key.
[30] Gyebek: Then she gets a question.
[31] Yuri Dora: She gets a question. And she gets to answer it.
[32] ¶ Walking home, he says the count to the dark. Twelve. In twelve days the king’s rite ends, and the tribute boat is already in Sabi.
[33] ¶ **In spring the tribute boat comes back from Sabi with news of the king. Gyebek has one question for it…!**
